## I. Pre - While - Post

### 1. Pre-stage

- Establish a purpose for reading + prior knowledge about the topic
- Improve vocabulary so students can complete the task successfully
- Predict what they're going to do

### 2. While-stage

- Activities that help students focus on aspects of the text + understand it better
- Help learners to deal with the text as they would in their first language

### 3. Post-stage

- Help students understand text further, by critically analyzing what they have read
- Reading comprehension, if one will

## II. Reading Activities

### 1. Pre-stage

- **Know - Want - Learn chart**: A chart about what they already Know before, what they Want to know during, and what they have Learned after the reading
- **True / False**: Ss read a few statements and decide if they are true or false, these statements will become relevant during the passage.
- **Videos**: Ss watch a short (3-5 minutes) video related to the topic, then discuss about the video. T can use this discussion as a lead-in to the passage.
- **Work in pairs**: Ss work in pairs to discuss about the topic before the passage.

### 2. While-stage

- **Identify topic sentences**: Ss find the topic sentences and infer the main idea from these sentences. Every paragraph should include a topic sentence identifying the main idea of the paragraph.
- **Distinguish between general and specific ideas**: i.e., _the general idea of the passage itself_, and the _specific idea of each paragraph._
- **Identify connectors**: Find linking words, conjunctions and see how they link ideas together within the text.
- **Coding text**: Ss mark sentences they don't understand or find interesting.

### 3. Post-stage

- **Creative discussions**: Prepare four or five simple questions and ask students to talk about those questions for 3 minutes. Afterwards, ask one member of each pair to go and talk to another person in the group.
- **Finding related texts/excerpts**: After students have finished reading, they can browse the internet for a new related to something they read.
  - For example: if they read something about morals and values, they can find examples of altruism on the web and they can share that information with their classmates.

| Post-reading                                                                                                                                                               | -To reinforce students’  understanding of the passage<br><br>-To further students’ understanding by relating the passage with themselves<br><br>-To familiarize students with the new vocabulary                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | - T splits class into pairs, then asks the class to discuss for 4-5 minutes: “Would you like to live in the Old Quarter?” and “Do you think it’s important to preserve ancient areas like the Old Quarter? Why or why not?”<br><br>- When time runs out, T calls a few students for responses, with correction and feedback as needed.<br><br>- Expected answers for Q1: Yes / No<br>    <br><br>- T asks Ss to explain why they would (not) like to live in the Old Quarter<br>    <br><br>- Expected answers for Q2: Yes / No<br>    <br><br>- Expected follow ups to yes: They are proofs of the country’s history / They play a big part in the country’s culture / Strong tourist attraction<br>    <br>- Expected follow ups for no: Cost a lot of money to maintain / Values slowly falling out of the times<br>    <br><br>- T wraps up the activity and summarizes the responses.
